 Tacony-Palmyra Bridge reopens hours after cargo ship crash 
 A large cargo ship crashed into the Tacony-Palmyra Bridge on Nov. 12 and traffic couldn't cross between Pennsylvania and New Jersey for hours. 
 By Emily Rose Grassi and Siobhan McGirl • 
 Published November 12, 2026 • 
 Updated on November 12, 2026 at 11:34 pm 
 BOOKMARKER 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 It took most of the day on Thursday for the Tacony-Palmyra Bridge to reopen after a cargo ship hit it. NBC10’s Miguel Martinez-Valle reports. 
 Traffic between Pennsylvania and New Jersey was disrupted for hours after a large cargo ship crashed into the Tacony-Palmyra Bridge on Thursday, according to Pa. State Rep. Ed Neilson.
 The crash happened around 1 p.m. on Nov. 12 when the bridge was open and the ship was passing underneath. 
 Stream Philadelphia News for free, 24/7, wherever you are with NBC10.
   WATCH HERE 
 Following the crash, the bridge sustained minor damage and drivers were being diverted to other routes.
 NBC10 saw crews evaluating the bridge structure as they lifted and lowered the draw bridge to inspect it. 
 The bridge was finally reopened to cars just before 9 p.m.
 The ship is currently moored in Fairless Hills and crews will be on the ground there to evaluate it for any potential damage. 
 Officials haven't said if the crash is weather-related but it happened as severe storms moved through the region.
